sections.overview: Jahu is a large South American freshwater catfish native to the Paraná–Paraguay basin.
sections.identification: It is a large pimelodid catfish; FishBase records a maximum of 140 cm standard length.
sections.habitat: Adults occupy deeper river reaches, while fry are found mainly near the mouths of smaller tributaries.
sections.diet: In a hatchery study, captive brood fish were fed live juvenile fishes.
sections.behavior: It is migratory and follows seasonal expansion of aquatic habitats during river flooding.
sections.reproduction: It is a total spawner; researchers have also induced spawning in hatchery-kept adults.
sections.ecology: Dams, overfishing, agriculture, mining, navigation and pollution have contributed to reduced catches in parts of its range.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global Near Threatened assessment dated 2020.

sources.title: Induced spawning and early ontogeny in hatchery-reared Zungaro jahu — SciELO
